description: Two silent-unless-relevant hook sets. The dashboard-kit notice: one line at session start or /clear in a repository that owns a Fabric service whose dashboard has no kit or an older one (fabric-dashboard/0.1, DEC-0036), phrased as an upgrade the agent may make itself. The Fabric session hooks (working-with-fabric, COM-04, FAA-12a): at session start or /clear, the preamble when Claude Code has the MCP server `fabric` and Fabric runs (fabric_whoami, then the project board through com.status and com.list, claim and release); when Fabric is down, one line, only in a project that uses Fabric (a Fabric contract file, a project-bound registration or a service descriptor naming the repository); nothing on compact or resume; each turn's facts (HEAD, files changed, lines added and removed, never content), the board's unread count, and, once the running Fabric's fabric_session_observe takes them, the other repositories the turn touched (the last 512 KB of the session transcript, message text included, is then read and only the current turn's tool names and path arguments are used; host/owner/name leave the machine, never a local path or text) and the session's end through Fabric, only when the running Fabric advertises session-hooks/1; at each prompt one line only when the unread count rose, then each nudge a turn's answer carried, once (watch-mail prints those of turns it delivered). All silent in a session Fabric launched. Every hook reads no Fabric token (a credential embedded in an origin URL is read by git config and dropped in memory, never spooled or sent), prints at most one block, always exits 0, and hands any Fabric call to a detached worker with a 10 s deadline.
